title: Home-Based Monitor for Gait and Activity Analysis
protocol: Check the suitcase contents to ensure inclusion of the docking station.
Include the power cord divided into two pieces for connection to a power supply.
Ensure presence of the Ethernet cable for interface with a router.
Pack the two sensors for daily activity recording.
Prepare bands suitable for attachment based on configuration and ambulatory status.
Provide one participant manual and one investigator manual.
Include one task reminder.
Add a screwdriver for USB key replacement.
Carry two blank USB keys.
Print and prepare the assignment form to record device allocation.
For non-ambulant patients, fix one sensor on the wrist.
Fix the second sensor on the wheelchair.
For ambulant participants, fix two sensors either on a wrist and an ankle or on both ankles.
For the wrist-ankle configuration, place one sensor on the wrist of the dominant hand using the provided bracelet so that the waves are pointing toward the fingers.
Place the second sensor on the ankle, on the same side as the wrist sensor, above the external malleolus with the waves pointing in the forward direction.
For the ankle-ankle configuration, place a sensor on each ankle, above the external malleolus with the waves pointing in the forward direction.
For non-ambulant participants, fix one sensor on the wrist and the other on the wheelchair.
Place one sensor on the wrist of the participant’s dominant hand using the provided bracelet so that the waves are pointing toward the fingers.
Attach the second sensor to a safe place on the wheelchair bag.
Explain daily routine for sensors’ use to the participant.
Plug the docking station into the power supply.
Attach the docking station to the router if an internet connection is available.
Insert the sensors into the docking station.
Localize the two light-emitting diodes (LEDs) on the docking station which indicate the status of the sensors.
Verify that the LEDs become orange when plugged into a power source, indicating sensor batteries are charging and data is being downloaded from the sensors to the USB drive.
Restart the procedure if the LEDS are still blinking after 5 min.
Contact the clinical site team if the issue persists.
Verify that the LEDs are green in the morning, indicating fully charged sensor batteries and cleared memory.
Remove the sensors from the docking station.
Wear the sensors as demonstrated by the evaluator.
If one or both sensors have orange LEDs after two consecutive days, contact the clinical center.
Wear the sensors throughout the day and place them back on the docking station at night.
Remove the sensors during activities involving water, special medical examinations (e.g., MRI, CT-scan, X-ray), or any activity that could damage them.
Keep the removed sensors in a safe place on a firm surface until resuming wear after the activity.
Tidy up all device items and return the device to the clinical center.
Encourage participants to wear sensors during normal daily activities.
Complete a dedicated assignment form.
Download data from sensors using the docking station at the end of each day.
Store downloaded data on a USB drive accessible only by evaluators.
Provide USB drives with capacity adjusted to recording period constraints.
Remove USB drive from docking station if not connected to internet.
Replace removed USB drive with a blank one at the end of the recording period.
Send the used USB drive to the support team for analysis.
Upload data to cloud storage if the docking station is connected to the internet.
Extract data from the cloud storage at selected time points during the study.
Analyze the extracted data using a dedicated algorithm.
Adjust the analysis periods based on the clinical study requirements.
Generate and adjust monitoring reports according to the clinical study needs.
